// THE CAPABILITY ITSELF: IMPORT IT AND GRANT ONE.
//
// Every gate in the layer is the same gate, so the obvious attack is to walk through it rather
// than around it: import the capability package and call Grant.
//
// This is the fixture that proves the whole mechanism, and it is the reason the classifiers live
// at server/triageclasses instead of under server/utils. Go's internal rule makes
// a/b/internal/c importable by everything rooted at a/b and by nothing else. The capability is at
// server/utils/internal/triagecap, so package utils and package triage can name it and this
// package cannot. While the classifiers lived at server/utils/triage/classes they were rooted at
// server/utils and the rule would have waved them straight through; moving the directory is what
// makes the compiler refuse.
package leakfixture

import "ars0n-framework-v2-server/utils/internal/triagecap"

func leakGrantYourself() triagecap.Runner {
	return triagecap.Grant()
}
